18.1.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.1.text: Arjuna said, O Mighty-armed One! I desire to know, in detail, the distinctive nature of renunciation and relinquishment, O Hrsikesa! O Slayer of Kesin!

18.1.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.1.text: Arjuna said, "I desire to know the truth about renunciation and abnegation separately, O Krishna."

18.1.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.1.text: Arjuna said, O mighty-armed Hrsikesa, O slayer of Kesi, I want to know separately the truth about sannyasa as well as about tyaga.

18.1.author: Swami Sivananda
18.1.text: Arjuna said, "O mighty-armed Hrishikesa, I desire to know the essence or truth of renunciation and abandonment severally, O slayer of Kesi."

18.1.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.1.text: Arjuna asked, "O Mighty One! I desire to know how relinquishment is distinguished from renunciation.

18.2.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.2.text: The Bhagavat said, "The seers understand the act of renouncing desire-motivated actions as renunciation; the experts declare the relinquishment of the fruits of all actions to be relinquishment."

18.2.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.2.text: The Lord said, "The sages hold that Sannyasa is the giving up of all works motivated by desire, and the wise declare Tyaga to be the abandonment of the fruits of all works.

18.2.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.2.text: The Blessed Lord said, "The learned ones know sannyasa to be the giving up of actions done with a desire for reward. The adepts call the abandonment of the results of all works 'tyaga'."

18.2.author: Swami Sivananda
18.2.text: The Blessed Lord said, "The sages understand sannyasa to be the renunciation of action with desire; the wise declare the abandonment of the fruits of all actions to be tyaga."

18.2.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.2.text: Lord Shri Krishna replied: The sages say that renunciation is forgoing an action that springs from desire, and relinquishing is the surrender of its fruit.

18.3.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.3.text: Certain wise men declare that the harmful action should be relinquished, while others say that the actions of performing sacrifices, giving gifts, and observing austerities should not be relinquished.

18.3.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.3.text: Some sages say that all actions should be abandoned as evil; others declare that works such as sacrifices, gifts, and austerities should not be abandoned.

18.3.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.3.text: Some learned persons say that action, beset with evil as it is, should be abandoned, and others say that the practice of sacrifice, charity, and austerity should not be abandoned.

18.3.author: Swami Sivananda
18.3.text: Some philosophers declare that actions should be abandoned as evil; while others declare that acts of sacrifice, gift, and austerity should not be relinquished.

18.3.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.3.text: Some philosophers say that all action is evil and should be abandoned, whereas others maintain that acts of sacrifice, benevolence, and austerity should not be given up.

18.4.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.4.text: O best of Bharata's descendants! Listen to My considered view about relinquishing: Indeed, the act of relinquishing is rightly spoken to be threefold, O best among men!

18.4.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.4.text: Listen to My decision, O Arjuna, concerning abandonment; for abandonment is declared to be of three kinds.

18.4.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.4.text: O the most excellent among the descendants of Bharata, hear from Me the firm conclusion regarding that tyaga. For, O greatest among men, tyaga has been clearly declared to be of three kinds.

18.4.author: Swami Sivananda
18.4.text: Hear from Me the conclusion or the final truth about this abandonment, O best of the Bharatas; abandonment, indeed, O best of men, has been declared to be of three kinds.

18.4.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.4.text: O best of Indians! Listen to my judgment regarding this problem. It has a threefold aspect.

18.5.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.5.text: The actions of Vedic sacrifice, gift, and austerity should not be relinquished and they must necessarily be performed; for the men of wisdom, the Vedic sacrifice, gift, and austerity are the means of purification.

18.5.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.5.text: The acts of sacrifice, gifts, and austerities should not be relinquished; but should be performed... ...For sacrifices, gifts, and austerities are the means of purification for the wise.

18.5.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.5.text: The practice of sacrifice, charity, and austerity should not be abandoned; it should certainly be undertaken. Sacrifice, charity, and austerity are indeed the purifiers of the wise.

18.5.author: Swami Sivananda
18.5.text: Acts of sacrifice, gift, and austerity should not be abandoned, but should be performed; for sacrifice, gift, and austerity are the purifiers of the wise.

18.5.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.5.text: Acts of sacrifice, benevolence, and austerity should not be given up, but should be performed, for they purify the aspiring soul.

18.6.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.6.text: Even these actions should be performed by relinquishing attachment and the fruits thereof; this is my considered best opinion, O son of Prtha!

18.6.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.6.text: It is My decided and final view that even these acts should be done, O Arjuna, with relinquishment of attachment and the forsaking of the fruits thereof.

18.6.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.6.text: But even these actions must be undertaken by renouncing attachment and hankering for results. This is My firm and definitive conclusion, O Partha.

18.6.author: Swami Sivananda
18.6.text: But even these actions should be performed, leaving aside attachment and the desire for rewards, O Arjuna; this is my certain and most assured conviction.

18.6.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.6.text: But they should be done with detachment and without thought of reward. This is my final judgement.

18.7.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.7.text: The renunciation of the enjoined action does not make sense; and completely relinquishing it, out of ignorance, is proclaimed on all sides as an act of Tamas (Strand).

18.7.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.7.text: But the renunciation of obligatory acts is not proper; abandonment of these through delusion is declared to be of a Tamasic nature.

18.7.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.7.text: Abandoning one's daily obligatory acts is not justifiable; giving up those through delusion is said to be rooted in tamas.

18.7.author: Swami Sivananda
18.7.text: Verily, the renunciation of obligatory action is not proper; the abandonment of the same out of delusion is declared to be Tamasic.

18.7.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.7.text: It is not right to give up actions which are obligatory; and if they are misunderstood, it is the result of sheer ignorance.

18.8.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.8.text: He who would, out of fear of bodily exertion, relinquish an action just because it is painful—that person, having thus made relinquishment an act of the Rajas (Strand), would not at all gain the fruit of that relinquishment.

18.8.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.8.text: He who renounces acts that are painful out of fear of bodily suffering performs a Rajasika abandonment; however, he does not gain the fruit of such abandonment.

18.8.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.8.text: Whatever action one may relinquish merely as being painful, out of fear of physical suffering, he, having resorted to renunciation based on rajas, will surely not acquire the fruits of renunciation.

18.8.author: Swami Sivananda
18.8.text: He who abandons action out of fear of bodily trouble (because it is painful), does not obtain the merit of renunciation by performing such Rajasic renunciation.

18.8.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.8.text: To avoid an action out of fear of physical suffering, as it is likely to be painful, is to act out of passion, and the benefit of renunciation will not be gained.

18.9.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.9.text: "This is a thing to be performed" - just on that ground, whatever usual action is performed, relinquishing attachment and also fruit - that act of relinquishment is deemed to be of the Sattva (strand).

18.9.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.9.text: When actions are performed as they ought to be done, O Arjuna, renouncing attachment and the results thereof, such abandonment is regarded as Sattvika.

18.9.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.9.text: Whatever obligatory duty is performed just because it is a bounden duty, O Arjuna, by giving up attachment and the results as well—that renunciation is considered to be based on sattva.

18.9.author: Swami Sivananda
18.9.text: Whatever obligatory action is done, O Arjuna, merely because it ought to be done, abandoning attachment and also the desire for reward, that renunciation is regarded as sattvic (pure).

18.9.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.9.text: He who performs an obligatory action, believing it to be a duty that ought to be done, without any personal desire to do the act or to receive any return—such renunciation is pure.

18.10.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.10.text: The man of renunciation, who is well-possessed of Sattva, is wise and has his doubts destroyed—he does not hate unskilled action and does not cling to skilled action.

18.10.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.10.text: One who has abandoned, imbued with Sattva, wise, and whose doubts have been dispelled—such a person neither hates disagreeable acts nor clings to agreeable ones.

18.10.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.10.text: The man of renunciation, imbued with sattva, wise and free from doubts, does not hate unbecoming action, nor does he become attached to becoming activity.

18.10.author: Swami Sivananda
18.10.text: The man of renunciation, pervaded by purity, intelligent, and with his doubts cut asunder, does not hate an unpleasant task nor is he attached to a pleasant one.

18.10.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.10.text: The wise man who has attained purity, whose doubts are resolved, who is filled with the spirit of self-abnegation, does not shy away from action due to its pain, nor does he crave it due to its pleasure.

18.11.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.11.text: Indeed, to relinquish actions entirely is not possible for a body-bearing one; but whoever relinquishes the fruits of actions, he is said to be a man of [true] relinquishment.

18.11.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.11.text: For, it is impossible for one who has a body to completely abandon actions. But he who gives up the results of his works is called the one who has abandoned them.

18.11.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.11.text: Since it is not possible for one who holds onto a body to give up actions entirely, therefore he who renounces the results of his actions is called a man of renunciation.

18.11.author: Swami Sivananda
18.11.text: Indeed, it is not possible for an embodied being to completely abandon actions; however, he who relinquishes the rewards of actions is truly called a man of renunciation.

18.11.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.11.text: But since those still in the body cannot entirely avoid action, in their case, the abandonment of the fruit of action is considered as complete renunciation.

18.12.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.12.text: The three-fold fruit of action—the undesired, the desired, and the mixed—accrues even after death to those who are not men of renunciation, but never to those who are men of renunciation.

18.12.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.12.text: Undesirable, desirable, and mixed—thus, threefold is the fruit of work that accrues after death to those who have not renounced; but to those who have renounced, none accrues whatsoever.

18.12.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.12.text: The threefold results of actions—the undesirable, the desirable, and the mixed—accrue after death to those who do not resort to renunciation, but never to those who resort to renunciation.

18.12.author: Swami Sivananda
18.12.text: The threefold fruit of action (evil, good, and mixed) accrues after death to those who do not abandon it, but never to those who do.

18.12.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.12.text: For those who cannot renounce all desires, the fruit of action hereafter is threefold—good, evil, and partly good and partly evil. But for him who has renounced, there is none.

18.13.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.13.text: O mighty-armed one! Learn from Me these five causes, declared in the conclusion of deliberations on proper knowledge, for the accomplishment of all actions.

18.13.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.13.text: Learn from Me, O Arjuna, these five causes for the accomplishment of all acts, as described in Sankhya-krtanta—the science of exact understanding of things—for the accomplishment of works.

18.13.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.13.text: O mighty-armed one, learn from Me these five factors for the accomplishment of all actions, which have been spoken of in the Vedanta, in which actions terminate.

18.13.author: Swami Sivananda
18.13.text: Learn from Me, O mighty-armed Arjuna, these five causes, as declared in the Sankhya system, for the accomplishment of all actions.

18.13.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.13.text: I will now tell you, O Mighty Man, the five causes that must come together, according to the final decision of philosophy, for an action to be accomplished.

18.14.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.14.text: The basis, the agent, the various instruments, the distinct activities of various kinds, and Destiny, which is the fifth factor, are all present.

18.14.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.14.text: The seat of action, the agent, the various kinds of organs, the different and distinctive functions of vital air, and the fifth among these—Divinity—all these.

18.14.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.14.text: The locus, the agent, the different kinds of organs, the many and varied activities, and the divine are the fifth here.

18.14.author: Swami Sivananda
18.14.text: The body, the doer, the various senses, the different functions of various kinds, and the presiding deity—the fifth.

18.14.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.14.text: They have a body, a personality, physical organs, and manifold activities and destinies.

18.15.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.15.text: O Arjuna! Whatever action is undertaken with the body, speech, or mind, whether it is lawful or otherwise, its factors are these five.

18.15.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.15.text: For whatever action a person undertakes with their body, speech, and mind, whether right or wrong, i.e., enjoined or forbidden by the Sastras, the following five are its causes:

18.15.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.15.text: Whatever action a person performs with their body, speech, and mind, whether it be just or its opposite, these five are the causes of it.

18.15.author: Swami Sivananda
18.15.text: Whatever action a person performs with their body, speech, and mind, whether right or wrong, these five are its causes.

18.15.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.15.text: Whatever action a person performs, whether by muscular effort, speech, or thought, and whether it be right or wrong, these five are the essential causes.

18.16.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.16.text: But this being the case, whoever views himself as the sole agent due to their imperfect intellect—they, the defective-minded ones, do not view things rightly.

18.16.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.16.text: Therefore, he who, due to his uncultivated understanding, perceives only the self as the agent, he of wicked mind does not truly perceive.

18.16.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.16.text: Therefore, anyone whose intellect is imperfect and perceives the Absolute Self as the agent, does not perceive properly and has a distorted intellect.

18.16.author: Swami Sivananda
18.16.text: Now, such being the case, verily he who, owing to an untrained understanding, looks upon his Self, which is isolated, as the agent, he of perverted intelligence does not see.

18.16.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.16.text: But the fool, who, due to his immature judgment, supposes that it is his own Self alone that acts, perverts the truth and does not see rightly.

18.17.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.17.text: He whose mental disposition is not dominated by the sense of 'I', and whose intellect is not stained—he, even if he slays these worlds, does not [really] slay any and is not fettered.

18.17.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.17.text: He who is free from the notion of 'I am the doer,' and whose understanding is not tainted, does not slay, even though he slays all these men, nor is he bound.

18.17.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.17.text: He who has no feeling of egoism, whose intellect is untainted, he does not kill, nor does he become bound—even by killing these creatures!

18.17.author: Swami Sivananda
18.17.text: He who is free from the egoistic notion, whose intelligence is not tainted by good or evil, though he slays these people, he does not slay, nor is he bound by the action.

18.17.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.17.text: He who has no pride and whose intellect is unalloyed by attachment, even though he kills these people, he does not kill them, and his act does not bind him.

18.18.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.18.text: The instrument of knowledge, the object of knowledge, and the knowing subject—the prompting in action, consisting of these threefold elements—is the proper grasping of action with threefold elements, namely, the instrument, the object, and the agent.

18.18.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.18.text: Knowledge, the object of knowledge, and the knower are the threefold incitements to action. The instrument, the act, and the agent are the threefold constituents of action.

18.18.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.18.text: Knowledge, the object of knowledge, and the knower—these are the threefold inducements to action. The comprehension of actions comes under three heads: the instruments, the object, and the subject.

18.18.author: Swami Sivananda
18.18.text: Knowledge, the knowable, and the knower form the threefold impulse for action; the organ, the action, and the agent form the threefold basis of action.

18.18.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.18.text: Knowledge, the knower, and the object of knowledge are the three incentives to action; and the act, the actor, and the instrument are the threefold constituents.

18.19.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.19.text: The instrument of knowledge, the object, and the agent are just three kinds due to the differences in the strands—thus it is declared in enumerating the strands. You must also listen to these [from Me] as they are.

18.19.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.19.text: Knowledge, action, and agent are declared in the science of the Gunas to be of three kinds, according to the difference in the Gunas. Listen to them also as they are.

18.19.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.19.text: Knowledge, action, and agent are stated in the teaching about the gunas to be only of three kinds, according to the differences of the gunas. Hear about them also as they are.

18.19.author: Swami Sivananda
18.19.text: Knowledge, action, and actor are declared in the science of the Gunas (Sankhya philosophy) to be of three kinds only, according to the distinction of the Gunas. Of these, hear duly.

18.19.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.19.text: The knowledge, the action, and the doer differ according to their qualities. Listen to this as well.

18.20.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.20.text: That instrument of knowledge, by means of which one perceives the singular, immutable existence in all beings, the unclassified among the classified ones—that you must know to be born of the Sattva (Strand).

18.20.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.20.text: Know that knowledge to be sattvika, by which one sees in all beings an immutable existence, undivided even in the divided.

18.20.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.20.text: Know that knowledge to originate from sattva, through which one sees a single, undecaying, undivided entity in all the diversified things.

18.20.author: Swami Sivananda
18.20.text: That by which one sees the indestructible Reality in all beings, not separate in any of them—know that knowledge to be Sattvic.

18.20.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.20.text: That knowledge which sees the One Indestructible in all beings, the One Indivisible in all separate lives, can be truly called Pure Knowledge.

18.21.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.21.text: That instrument of knowledge, by means of which one considers the varied natures of different sorts in all beings as truly distinct—that is regarded to be of the Rajas strand.

18.21.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.21.text: But that knowledge which sees all beings, due to their individual nature, as distinct entities—know that knowledge to be Rajasic.

18.21.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.21.text: But know that knowledge to originate from rajas, which amidst all things apprehends the different entities of various kinds as distinct [as possessing distinct selves].

18.21.author: Swami Sivananda
18.21.text: But that knowledge which sees in all beings various entities of distinct kinds as being distinct from one another, know thou that knowledge to be Rajasic.

18.21.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.21.text: The knowledge that perceives the manifold existence in all beings as separate comes from passion.

18.22.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.22.text: That [instrument-of-knowledge], because of which one, not realizing the whole, gets indulged without reason in a particular activity, and which is unconcerned with the real nature of things and is insignificant—that is declared to be of the Tamas (Strand).

18.22.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.22.text: But that knowledge is declared to be Tamasika which clings to one single act as if it were the whole, which is not based on reason, and which is false and insignificant.

18.22.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.22.text: But that (knowledge) is said to be born of tamas which is confined to one form as if it were all, which is irrational, unconcerned with truth, and trivial.

18.22.author: Swami Sivananda
18.22.text: But that which clings to one single effect as if it were the whole, without reason, without any foundation in Truth, and is trivial—that is declared to be Tamasic.

18.22.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.22.text: But that which clings blindly to one idea as if it were all, without logic, truth, or insight, has its origin in darkness.

18.23.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.23.text: The object that has been acquired with determination, without attachment and without desire or hatred, by one who does not crave to reap the fruit of their action - that is declared to be of the Sattva (Strand).

18.23.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.23.text: That obligatory act is said to be Sattvika, which is done without attachment, without desire or aversion, and by one who seeks no fruit.

18.23.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.23.text: The daily obligatory action which is performed without attachment and without likes or dislikes, by one who does not hanker for rewards, is said to be born of sattva.

18.23.author: Swami Sivananda
18.23.text: An action that is ordained, free from attachment, done without love or hatred, and without desire for reward is declared to be Sattvic.

18.23.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.23.text: An obligatory action done by one who is disinterested, who neither likes nor dislikes it, and gives no thought to the consequences that may follow, such an action is Pure.

18.24.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.24.text: The object which is abundant in afflictions and which is further desired by one who craves to attain the desired thing with the feeling of 'I'—that is considered to be of the Rajas (Strand).

18.24.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.24.text: But that act is said to be Rajasic, which is performed with great effort by one who seeks to gratify their desires and under the prompting of egoism.

18.24.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.24.text: But that action is said to be born of rajas which is done by one desirous of results or by one who is egotistical, and which is highly strenuous.

18.24.author: Swami Sivananda
18.24.text: But that action which is done by one longing for the fulfillment of desires or gain with egotism or with much effort is declared to be Rajasic (passionate).

18.24.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.24.text: But even though an action involves the most strenuous endeavor, yet if the doer is seeking to gratify their desires and is filled with personal vanity, it may be assumed to originate in passion.

18.25.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.25.text: The object which is gained, due to ignorance, without considering the result, the loss, the injury to others, and one's own strength—that is declared to be of the Tamas (Strand).

18.25.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.25.text: That act is said to be Tamasika which is undertaken through delusion, without regard to consequences, loss, injury, and one's own capacity.

18.25.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.25.text: That action is said to be born of tamas which is undertaken out of delusion, without consideration of its consequences, loss, harm, and ability.

18.25.author: Swami Sivananda
18.25.text: That action which is undertaken from delusion, without regard for the consequences, loss, injury, and one's own ability, is declared to be Tamasic (dark).

18.25.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.25.text: An action undertaken through delusion, with no regard to the spiritual implications, the capacity of the doer, or the potential harm that may follow, is assumed to be a product of ignorance.

18.26.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.26.text: The agent who is free from attachment, who does not make any speech of egoism, who is full of contentment and enthusiasm, and who does not change mentally in success or failure—that agent is said to be of the Sattva nature.

18.26.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.26.text: That agent is said to be Sattvika, who is free from attachment, who does not boast of himself, who is endowed with steadiness and zeal, and who is unaffected by success and failure.

18.26.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.26.text: [Ast. introduces this verse with 'Idanim kartrbhedah ucyate, Now is being stated the distinctions among the agents.'-Tr.] The agent who is free from attachment [Attachment to results or the idea of agentship.], not egotistical, endowed with fortitude and diligence, and unperturbed by success and failure is said to be possessed of sattva.

18.26.author: Swami Sivananda
18.26.text: An agent who is free from attachment, non-egoistic, endowed with firmness and enthusiasm, and unaffected by success or failure, is considered to be of a Sattvic (pure) nature.

18.26.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.26.text: But when a person has no sentiment or ego, when they possess courage and confidence, not caring whether they succeed or fail, then their action arises from purity.

18.27.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.27.text: The agent, who is a man of passion, who craves the fruit of his actions, and is avaricious; who is injurious by nature, impure, and is overpowered by joy and grief—that agent is proclaimed to be of the Rajas (Strand).

18.27.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.27.text: That doer is called Rajasika who is passionate, who seeks the fruits of his actions, who is greedy, harmful, and impure, and who is swayed by delight and grief.

18.27.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.27.text: The agent who has attachment, who is desirous of the results of actions, covetous, cruel by nature, unclean, and subject to joy and sorrow, is declared to be possessed of rajas.

18.27.author: Swami Sivananda
18.27.text: Passionate, desiring to obtain the reward of their actions, greedy, cruel, impure, moved by joy and sorrow, such an agent is said to be Rajasic.

18.27.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.27.text: In one who is impulsive, greedy, looking for reward, violent, impure, and torn between joy and sorrow, it may be assumed that Passion is predominant.

18.28.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.28.text: The agent who does not exert is vulgar, obstinate, and deceitful; they are a man of wickedness and are lazy, sorrowful, and procrastinating—such an agent is said to be of the Tamas strand.

18.28.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.28.text: That doer is said to be Tamasika who is unqualified, unrefined, obstinate, depraved, dishonest, indolent, despondent, and lethargic.

18.28.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.28.text: The agent who is unsteady, naive, inflexible, deceitful, wicked, lazy, sullen, and procrastinating is said to be possessed of tamas.

18.28.author: Swami Sivananda
18.28.text: Unsteady, vulgar, inflexible, deceitful, malicious, lazy, despondent, and procrastinating—such an agent is called Tamasic.

18.28.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.28.text: While he whose purpose is weak, who is low-minded, stubborn, dishonest, malicious, lazy, despondent, and procrastinating—he may be assumed to be in darkness.

18.29.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.29.text: You must listen to Me as I expound the three-fold division of the intellect and content, both completely and individually, based on the Strands, O Dhananjaya!

18.29.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.29.text: Hear now, O Arjuna, the threefold division of Buddhi (reason) and Dhrti (fortitude) according to the Gunas, to be fully and severally set forth.

18.29.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.29.text: O Dhananjaya, listen to the classification of the intellect and fortitude, which is threefold according to the gunas, while it is being stated in detail and separately.

18.29.author: Swami Sivananda
18.29.text: Hear thou the threefold division of intellect and firmness, according to the Gunas, as I declare them fully and distinctly, O Arjuna.

18.29.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.29.text: Reason and conviction are threefold, according to the quality that is dominant. I will explain them fully and separately, O Arjuna!

18.30.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.30.text: The intellect which knows the activity and the cessation from activity, the proper and improper actions, the fear and non-fear, and the bondage and emancipation—that intellect is considered to be of the Sattva (Strand).

18.30.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.30.text: That Buddhi, O Arjuna, which knows activity and renunciation, what should be done and what should not be done, fear and fearlessness, bondage and release—that Buddhi is Sattvika.

18.30.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.30.text: O Partha, that intellect is born of sattva which understands action and withdrawal, duty and what is not duty, the sources of fear and fearlessness, as well as bondage and freedom.

18.30.author: Swami Sivananda
18.30.text: The intellect which knows the path of work and renunciation, what should be done and what should not be done, fear and fearlessness, bondage and liberation—that intellect is Sattvic (pure), O Arjuna.

18.30.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.30.text: That intellect which understands the creation and dissolution of life, what actions should be done and what not, which discriminates between fear and fearlessness, bondage and deliverance, is Pure.

18.31.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.31.text: The intellect, by means of which one decides incorrectly between the righteous and the unrighteous, and what is a proper action and an improper one—that intellect is of the Rajas, O son of Prtha!

18.31.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.31.text: The Buddhi that gives an erroneous knowledge of Dharma and Adharma (its opposite) and also of what should be done and what should not be done, O Arjuna, is Rajasic.

18.31.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.31.text: O Partha, that intellect is born of rajas with which one wrongly understands virtue and vice, as well as what ought to be done and ought not to be done.

18.31.author: Swami Sivananda
18.31.text: That by which one wrongly understands dharma and adharma, and also what ought to be done and what ought not to be done—that intellect, O Arjuna, is rajasic (passionate).

18.31.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.31.text: The intellect that does not understand what is right and wrong, and what should be done and not done, is under the sway of Passion.

18.32.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.32.text: The intellect which, containing darkness (ignorance), conceives the unrighteous one as righteous and all things topsy-turvy—that intellect is deemed to be of the Tamas (Strand).

18.32.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.32.text: That Buddhi, O Arjuna, which, enveloped in darkness, regards Adharma as Dharma and reverses every value, is Tamasika.

18.32.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.32.text: O Partha, that intellect is born of tamas which, being covered by darkness, considers vice as virtue, and indeed perceives all things contrary to what they are.

18.32.author: Swami Sivananda
18.32.text: That intellect, O Arjuna, which is enveloped in darkness and sees Adharma as Dharma and all things perverted, is Tamasic (dark).

18.32.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.32.text: And that which, shrouded in Ignorance, thinks wrong to be right, and sees everything perversely, O Arjuna, that intellect is ruled by Darkness.

18.33.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.33.text: The unfailing content, by which one restrains, through Yoga, the activities of the mind, the living breath, and the senses, is considered to be of the Sattva (strand).

18.33.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.33.text: That fortitude, by which one maintains the unwavering activities of the mind and vital force, and these sense-organs, through yoga—that fortitude is of the nature of sattva.

18.33.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.33.text: O Partha, the firmness that is unfailing through concentration, with which one restrains the functions of the mind, vital forces, and the organs—that firmness is born of sattva.

18.33.author: Swami Sivananda
18.33.text: The unwavering firmness, through which Yoga restrains the functions of the mind, life-force, and senses—that firmness, O Arjuna, is Sattvic (pure).

18.33.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.33.text: The conviction and steady concentration with which the mind, the energy, and the senses are controlled—O Arjuna!—are the result of purity.

18.34.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.34.text: O Arjuna! The contentment by which one restrains one's bounden duty, pleasure, and wealth, and consequently desires the fruits of action—that contentment is of the Rajas strand, O son of Prtha!

18.34.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.34.text: That dhṛti, O Arjuna, by which one, who is desirous of fruits, longs for them with intense attachment and holds fast to duty, desire, and wealth—that dhṛti is rajasika.

18.34.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.34.text: But, O Partha, the steadfastness with which one holds on to righteousness, covetable things, and wealth, desiring their fruits as the occasion for each arises, that steadfastness is born of rajas.

18.34.author: Swami Sivananda
18.34.text: But that, O Arjuna, by which one holds fast to Dharma (duty), enjoyment of pleasures, and earning of wealth, on account of attachment and desire for reward—that firmness, O Arjuna, is Rajasic (passionate).

18.34.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.34.text: The conviction that always holds fast to rituals, self-interest, and wealth for the sake of what they may bring forth comes from passion.

18.35.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.35.text: The contentment where a foolish man does not give up his sleep, fear, grief, despondency, and arrogance—that contentment is deemed to be of the Tamas (Strand).

18.35.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.35.text: That Dhrti, by which a foolish person does not give up sleep, fear, grief, depression, and passion, O Arjuna, is of the nature of Tamas.

18.35.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.35.text: That firmness is considered to be born of tamas, due to which a person with a corrupt intellect does not give up sleep, fear, sorrow, despondency, as well as sensuality.

18.35.author: Swami Sivananda
18.35.text: That firmness, O Arjuna, by which a stupid man does not abandon sleep, fear, grief, despair, and conceit, is Tamasic.

18.35.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.35.text: And that which clings perversely to false idealism, fear, grief, despair, and vanity is the product of ignorance.

18.36.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.36.text: O best among the Bharatas! Now, you must also listen to Me about the three-fold happiness, wherein one delights in practice and attains the end of suffering.

18.36.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.36.text: Now hear from Me, O Arjuna, the threefold division of pleasure that in which one rejoices through long practice and in which one comes to the end of pain.

18.36.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.36.text: Now hear from Me, O scion of the Bharata dynasty, as regards the three kinds of joy: That in which one delights due to habit, and certainly attains the cessation of sorrows; [S. and S.S. take the second line of this verse along with the next verse referring to sattvika happiness.-Tr.]

18.36.author: Swami Sivananda
18.36.text: And now, O Arjuna, hear from Me of the threefold pleasure, in which one rejoices through practice and surely comes to the end of pain.

18.36.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.36.text: Hear further the three kinds of pleasure. That which increases day by day delivers one from misery.

18.37.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.37.text: [The happiness] which is like poison in the moment but is like nectar in the result—that happiness, born of serenity of the soul and intellect, you must know to be of the sattva (strand).

18.37.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.37.text: That which, at first, is like a poison but becomes like an elixir in the end, born from the serene state of mind focused on the Self—such pleasure is said to be Sattvika.

18.37.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.37.text: That which is like poison in the beginning, but is likened to nectar in the end, and which arises from the purity of one's intellect—that joy is spoken of as born of sattva.

18.37.author: Swami Sivananda
18.37.text: That which is like poison at first but in the end like nectar—that happiness is declared to be sattvic, born of the purity of one's own mind due to self-realization.

18.37.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.37.text: Which at first seems like poison but afterwards acts like nectar—that pleasure is pure, for it is born of wisdom.

18.38.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.38.text: [The happiness] which is like nectar at its due time due to the contact between the senses and sense-objects; but which is like poison at the time of its result—that is considered to be of the Rajas (Strand).

18.38.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.38.text: That pleasure which arises from the contact of senses with their objects, which is like elixir at first but like poison in the end, is said to be Rajasic.

18.38.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.38.text: That joy is referred to as born of rajas, which, arising from the contact of the organs and their objects, is like nectar in the beginning but like poison in the end.

18.38.author: Swami Sivananda
18.38.text: That happiness which arises from the contact of the senses with the objects, which is initially like nectar but eventually like poison, is said to be Rajasic.

18.38.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.38.text: That which, at first, is like nectar, as the senses revel in their objects, but in the end acts like poison—that pleasure arises from Passion.

18.39.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.39.text: The happiness that, both initially and subsequently, is of the nature of deluding the Self; and which results from sleep, indolence, and heedlessness—that is stated to be of the Tamas (Strand).

18.39.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.39.text: That pleasure which, at the beginning and end, deludes the self, through sleep, sloth, and error, is declared to be tamasic.

18.39.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.39.text: That joy is said to be born of tamas, which, both in the beginning and in the end, is delusive to oneself and arises from sleep, laziness, and inadvertence.

18.39.author: Swami Sivananda
18.39.text: That happiness which at first, as well as in the end, deludes the self, and which arises from sleep, indolence, and heedlessness—that is declared to be Tamasic.

18.39.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.39.text: While the pleasure that drugs the senses from start to finish, which springs from indolence, lethargy, and folly—that pleasure flows from Ignorance.

18.40.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.40.text: Whether on earth or among the gods in heaven, there is not a single being that is free from these three strands born of material nature.

18.40.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.40.text: There is no creature, on earth or among the gods in heaven, that is exempt from these three Gunas born of Prakrti.

18.40.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.40.text: There is no entity in the world, nor among the gods in heaven, that can be free from these three gunas born of Nature.

18.40.author: Swami Sivananda
18.40.text: There is no being on earth or in heaven among the gods that is liberated from the three qualities born of Nature.

18.40.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.40.text: There is nothing anywhere on earth or in the higher worlds that is free from the three Qualities, for they are born of Nature.

18.41.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.41.text: The duties of the Brahmanas, the Kshatriyas, the Vaishyas, and the Shudras are properly classified according to the qualities that are the sources of their nature, O scorcher of foes!

18.41.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.41.text: The duties of the Brahmanas, Ksatriyas, Vaisyas, and Sudras are clearly divided, O Arjuna, according to their Gunas, born of their nature.

18.41.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.41.text: O scorcher of enemies, the duties of the Brahmanas, Ksatriyas, Vaisyas, and Sudras have been fully classified according to the gunas born from Nature.

18.41.author: Swami Sivananda
18.41.text: Of Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, Vaisyas, and Sudras, O Arjuna, the duties are distributed according to the qualities born of their own nature.

18.41.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.41.text: O Arjuna! The duties of spiritual teachers, the soldiers, the traders, and the servants have all been fixed according to the dominant quality in their nature.

18.42.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.42.text: Quietude, self-control, purity, forbearance, straightforwardness, knowledge, wisdom, and faith in another world are the duties of the Brahmanas, born of their nature.

18.42.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.42.text: The control of the senses and mind, austerity, purity, forbearance, uprightness, knowledge, special knowledge, and faith—all these constitute the duty of a Brahmana, born of his inherent nature.

18.42.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.42.text: The natural duties of the Brahmanas are the control of the internal and external organs, austerity, purity, forgiveness, straightforwardness, knowledge, as well as wisdom [Knowledge refers to the understanding of subjects presented by the scriptures; wisdom means making them matters of one's own experience.], and faith.

18.42.author: Swami Sivananda
18.42.text: Serenity, self-restraint, austerity, purity, forgiveness, and uprightness, as well as knowledge, realization, and belief in God, are the duties of Brahmanas, born of their own nature.

18.42.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.42.text: Serenity, self-restraint, austerity, purity, forgiveness, uprightness, knowledge, wisdom, and faith in God—these constitute the duty of a spiritual teacher.

18.43.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.43.text: Heroic deeds, fiery energy, firmness, dexterity, and also non-attachment form the duties of the Ksatriyas, born of their nature, in battle, giving gifts, and overlordship.

18.43.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.43.text: Valor, invincibility, steadiness, dexterity, and not fleeing in battle, generosity, and regality are the duties of a Kshatriya, born of his inherent nature.

18.43.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.43.text: The natural duties of the Ksatriyas are heroism, boldness, fortitude, capability, and not retreating from battle, generosity, and lordliness.

18.43.author: Swami Sivananda
18.43.text: Prowess, splendor, firmness, dexterity, and not fleeing from battle, generosity, and lordliness are the duties of the Kshatriyas, born of their own nature.

18.43.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.43.text: Valor, glory, firmness, skill, generosity, steadiness in battle, and the ability to rule—these constitute the duty of a soldier. They flow from his own nature.

18.44.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.44.text: Ploughing, tending to cattle, and trading are the actions of the Vaisyas, born of their nature. The action of service is of the Sudras, born of their nature.

18.44.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.44.text: Agriculture, cattle-breeding, and trade are the duties of the Vaisya, born of their nature. And the duty of a Sudra is one of service, born of their nature.

18.44.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.44.text: The natural duties of the Vaisyas are agriculture, cattle-rearing, and trading. The natural duty of the Sudras, too, is in the form of service.

18.44.author: Swami Sivananda
18.44.text: Agriculture, cattle-rearing, and trade are the duties of the Vaisya (merchant), born of their own nature; and service is the duty of the Sudra (servant-class), born of their own nature.

18.44.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.44.text: Agriculture, the protection of cows, and trade are the duties of a trader, in accordance with his nature. The duty of a servant is to serve, which also agrees with his nature.

18.45.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.45.text: A person, devoted to their own respective action, attains success. How one attains success through devotion to their own action, that you must hear from Me.

18.45.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.45.text: Devoting oneself to one's duty, one attains perfection. Hear now how one devoted to their own duty attains perfection.

18.45.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.45.text: Being devoted to his own duty, one attains complete success. Hear how one devoted to their own duty achieves success.

18.45.author: Swami Sivananda
18.45.text: Each person devoted to their own duty attains perfection. How they attain perfection while being engaged in their own duty, hear now.

18.45.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.45.text: Perfection is attained when one diligently attends to their duty. Listen, and I will tell you how it is attained by one who always minds their own duty.

18.46.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.46.text: From whence the activities of the beings arise, and by which this universe is pervaded—worshipping That by one's own prescribed action, one attains success.

18.46.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.46.text: From whom all beings arise and by whom all this is pervaded—by worshipping Him with one's own duty, one reaches perfection.

18.46.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.46.text: A human being achieves success by adoring, through his own duties, Him from whom is the origin of creatures and by whom all this is pervaded.

18.46.author: Swami Sivananda
18.46.text: He from whom all the beings have evolved and by whom all this is pervaded, worshipping Him with his own duty, one attains perfection.

18.46.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.46.text: One reaches perfection by dedicating their actions to God, Who is the source of all being and fills everything.

18.47.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.47.text: Better is one's own prescribed duties, born of one's nature, even though it is devoid of excellence, than another's duty well executed; the doer of duty, dependent on one's own nature, does not incur sin.

18.47.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.47.text: Better is one's own duty, though ill done, than the duty of another, though well-performed. When one does the duty ordained by their own nature, they incur no stain.

18.47.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.47.text: One's own duty, though defective, is superior to another's duty well performed. By performing a duty according to one's own nature, one does not incur sin.

18.47.author: Swami Sivananda
18.47.text: Better is one's own duty, even if it is destitute of merits, than the duty of another well performed. He who does the duty ordained by his own nature incurs no sin.

18.47.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.47.text: It is better to do one's own duty, however defective it may be, than to follow the duty of another, however well one may perform it. He who does his duty as his own nature reveals it, never commits a sin.

18.48.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.48.text: O son of Kunti! One should not give up their nature-born duty, even if it appears to be defective. For, all beginnings are enveloped by harm, just as fire is by smoke.

18.48.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.48.text: One should not relinquish one's work, O Arjuna, though it may be imperfect; for, all endeavors are enveloped by imperfections as fire is by smoke.

18.48.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.48.text: O son of Kunti, one should not give up the duty to which one is born, even though it be imperfect. For all undertakings are surrounded by evil, as fire is with smoke.

18.48.author: Swami Sivananda
18.48.text: One should not, O Arjuna, abandon the duty to which one is born, though it may be faulty; for, all undertakings are enveloped by evil, just as fire is by smoke.

18.48.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.48.text: The duty that falls to one's lot of its own accord should not be abandoned, though it may have its defects. All acts are marred by defects, just as fire is obscured by smoke.

18.49.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.49.text: He, whose mind entertains no attachment to anything, who is self-controlled and is free from craving—he attains, by means of renunciation, the supreme success of actionlessness.

18.49.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.49.text: He whose understanding is unattached on all sides, whose self is controlled, who is free from desires—he attains the supreme perfection transcending all activity through renunciation.

18.49.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.49.text: He whose intellect remains unattached to everything, who has conquered his internal organs and is desireless, attains through monasticism the supreme perfection consisting of the state of one free from duties.

18.49.author: Swami Sivananda
18.49.text: He whose intellect is unattached everywhere, who has subdued his self, from whom desire has fled, he attains the supreme state of freedom from action through renunciation.

18.49.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.49.text: He whose mind is entirely detached, who has conquered himself, and whose desires have vanished, reaches that stage of perfect freedom through his renunciation, where action completes itself and leaves no seed.

18.50.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.50.text: Having attained success, how one attains Brahman—an attainment which is confirmed to be the final beatitude of true knowledge—that you must learn from Me briefly.

18.50.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.50.text: Learn from me, O Arjuna, in brief how one who has attained perfection attains the Brahman—the supreme consummation of knowledge.

18.50.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.50.text: Understand for certain from Me, in brief indeed, O son of Kunti, that process by which one who has achieved success attains Brahman, which is the supreme consummation of knowledge.

18.50.author: Swami Sivananda
18.50.text: Learn from Me, O Arjuna, in brief how one who has attained perfection reaches Brahman—the Eternal, that supreme state of knowledge.

18.50.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.50.text: I will now state briefly how one who has reached perfection finds the Eternal Spirit, the state of Supreme Wisdom.

18.51.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.51.text: He who has attained a completely pure intellect by firmly controlling his mind and renouncing sense-objects, sound, and driving out desire and hatred;

18.51.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.51.text: Endowed with a purified understanding, subduing the mind with steadiness, relinquishing sound and other objects of the senses and casting aside love and hate;

18.51.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.51.text: Endowed with a pure intellect and controlling oneself with fortitude, one should reject the objects beginning from sound [sound, touch, form, color, taste, and smell - Tr.] and eliminate attachment and hatred.

18.51.author: Swami Sivananda
18.51.text: Endowed with a pure intellect, controlling the self through firmness, relinquishing sound and other objects and abandoning attraction and hatred.

18.51.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.51.text: Guided always by pure reason, bravely restraining himself, renouncing the objects of sense and giving up attachment and hatred; he attains peace.

18.52.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.52.text: Who enjoys solitude, eats sparingly, has controlled their speech, body, and mind; who is devoted to the practice of meditation and yoga; and who has taken refuge in perpetual desirelessness;

18.52.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.52.text: Resorting to solitude, eating sparingly, restraining speech, body, and mind, ever engaged in the yoga of meditation and taking refuge in dispassion;

18.52.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.52.text: One who resorts to solitude, eats sparingly, has control over their speech, body, and mind, for whom meditation and concentration are ever the highest duty, and who is possessed of dispassion;

18.52.author: Swami Sivananda
18.52.text: Dwelling in solitude, eating sparingly, with speech, body, and mind subdued, always engaged in meditation and concentration, and resorting to dispassion.

18.52.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.52.text: Enjoying solitude, being abstemious, having his body, mind, and speech under perfect control, and being absorbed in meditation, he becomes free—always filled with the spirit of renunciation.

18.53.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.53.text: Relinquishing egotism, violence, pride, desire, wrath, and the sense of possession - he, the unselfish and calm one, is capable of becoming the Brahman.

18.53.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.53.text: Forsaking egoism, power, pride, desire, wrath, and possessions, with no feeling of 'mine' and tranquil, he becomes worthy of the state of Brahman.

18.53.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.53.text: Having discarded egotism, force, pride, desire, anger, and superfluous possessions, and being free from the idea of possession and serene, that person is fit for becoming Brahman.

18.53.author: Swami Sivananda
18.53.text: Having abandoned egoism, strength, arrogance, desire, anger, and covetousness, and being free from the notion of 'mine' and peaceful, he is fit for becoming Brahman.

18.53.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.53.text: Having abandoned selfishness, power, arrogance, anger, and desire, possessing nothing of his own, and having attained peace, he is fit to join the Eternal Spirit.

18.54.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.54.text: Having become the Brahman, the serene-minded one neither grieves nor rejoices; remaining equal to all beings, he gains the highest devotion to Me.

18.54.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.54.text: Having realized the state of Brahman, tranquil, he neither grieves nor craves. Regarding all beings alike, he attains supreme devotion to Me.

18.54.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.54.text: One who has become Brahman and has attained the blissful Self does not grieve nor desire. Becoming the same towards all beings, he attains supreme devotion to Me.

18.54.author: Swami Sivananda
18.54.text: Becoming Brahman, serene in the Self, he neither grieves nor desires; he is the same to all beings, and obtains supreme devotion to Me.

18.54.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.54.text: When he unites with the Eternal and his soul knows the bliss of the Self, he feels no desire or regret, he regards all beings equally, and enjoys the blessing of supreme devotion to Me.

18.55.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.55.text: Through devotion he comes to know of Me: Who I am and how, in fact, I am—having correctly known Me, he enters into Me. Then afterwards,

18.55.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.55.text: Through devotion, he comes to know Me fully—who and what I am in reality, who I am and how I am. Knowing Me thus in truth, he forthwith enters into Me.

18.55.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.55.text: Through devotion, he knows Me in reality, as to what and who I am. Then, having known Me truly, he enters into Me immediately afterward.

18.55.author: Swami Sivananda
18.55.text: By devotion, he knows Me in truth, who and what I am; then, having known Me in truth, he immediately enters into the Supreme.

18.55.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.55.text: By such devotion, he sees Me, who I am and what I am; and thus realizing the truth, he enters into My kingdom.

18.56.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.56.text: Performing all his actions all the time and taking refuge in Me, he attains, through My grace, the eternal, changeless state.

18.56.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.56.text: Taking refuge in Me and performing all works constantly, one, by My grace, attains the eternal and immutable abode.

18.56.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.56.text: Ever engaging in all actions, one to whom I am the refuge, attains the eternal, immutable state through my grace.

18.56.author: Swami Sivananda
18.56.text: Having taken refuge in Me and doing all actions, by My grace he obtains the eternal, indestructible state of being.

18.56.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.56.text: Relying on Me in all his actions and doing them for My sake, he attains, by My grace, eternal and unchangeable life.

18.57.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.57.text: Hence, O descendant of Bharata, renounce all actions in Me by your mind and take hold of the knowledge-Yoga. Always keep your thought-organ directed towards Me.

18.57.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.57.text: Surrender all your actions to Me with your mind, keep Me as your goal, and practice Buddhi-yoga, focusing your thoughts on Me always.

18.57.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.57.text: Mentally surrendering all actions to Me and accepting Me as the supreme, keep your mind ever fixed on Me by resorting to the concentration of your intellect.

18.57.author: Swami Sivananda
18.57.text: Mentally renouncing all actions in Me, having Me as the highest goal, and resorting to the yoga of discrimination, do thou ever fix thy mind on Me.

18.57.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.57.text: Surrender your actions to Me, live in Me, focus your intellect on Me, and always think of Me.

18.58.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.58.text: Having your thought-organ turned towards Me, you shall pass over all obstacles by My Grace. On the other hand, if you don't give up your sense of ego, you will not liberate yourself; instead, you will perish.

18.58.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.58.text: Focusing your thoughts on Me, you shall, by My grace, cross over all difficulties. If, however, out of self-conceit, you do not heed Me, you will perish.

18.58.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.58.text: Having your mind fixed on Me, you will cross over all difficulties by My grace. If, however, you do not listen out of egotism, you will be destroyed.

18.58.author: Swami Sivananda
18.58.text: Fixing your mind on Me, you shall, by My grace, overcome all obstacles; but if you will not hear Me due to egoism, you shall perish.

18.58.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.58.text: Fix your mind on Me, and by My grace you will overcome the obstacles in your path. But if, misled by pride, you do not listen, then you will indeed be lost.

18.59.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.59.text: In case, holding fast to the sense of ego, you think, 'I shall not fight,' that resolve of yours will be useless. Your own natural condition will incite you to fight.

18.59.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.59.text: If, in your self-conceit, you think, 'I will not fight,' your resolve is futile. Nature will compel you.

18.59.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.59.text: Though you think 'I shall not fight', relying on egotism, this determination of yours is vain. Your nature will impel you!

18.59.author: Swami Sivananda
18.59.text: If, filled with egoism, thou thinkest, "I will not fight," then thy resolve is vain; nature will compel thee.

18.59.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.59.text: If you in your vanity think of avoiding this fight, your will shall not be fulfilled, for Nature herself will compel you.

18.60.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.60.text: O son of Kunti! Being firmly bound by your own duty, born of your own nature, and thus not being independent, you would perform what you do not wish to do, due to your delusion.

18.60.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.60.text: O Arjuna, bound by your own duty born out of your own inner disposition, and having no control over your own will, you will be compelled to do that very thing which you now do not desire to do through delusion.

18.60.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.60.text: Being bound by your own duty, born of nature, O son of Kunti, you will, being helpless, verily do that which you do not wish to do, owing to indiscretion.

18.60.author: Swami Sivananda
18.60.text: O Arjuna, bound by your own Karma (action) born of your own nature, that which from delusion you wish not to do, even that you shall do helplessly.

18.60.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.60.text: O Arjuna! Your duty binds you. It has arisen from your own nature, and that which you do not desire to do in your delusion, you will do that very thing. You are helpless.

18.61.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.61.text: O Arjuna! This Lord dwells in the hearts of all beings, causing, by His trick of illusion, all beings to whirl round as if they are mounted on a revolving mechanical contrivance.

18.61.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.61.text: The Lord, O Arjuna, abides in the heart of every being, spinning them round and round, as if mounted on a wheel, by His power.

18.61.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.61.text: O Arjuna, the Lord resides in the region of the hearts of all creatures, revolving through Maya all the creatures as though mounted on a machine!

18.61.author: Swami Sivananda
18.61.text: The Lord dwells in the hearts of all beings, O Arjuna, causing all beings, by His illusory power, to revolve as if mounted on a machine.

18.61.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.61.text: God dwells in the hearts of all beings, O Arjuna! He causes them to revolve, as it were, on a wheel, by His mystic power.

18.62.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.62.text: To Him alone, O descendant of Bharata, you must go for refuge with all your thoughts. Through My grace, you will attain success and the eternal abode.

18.62.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.62.text: Seek refuge in Him alone, O Arjuna, with the entirety of your being. By His grace, you shall find supreme peace and an eternal abode.

18.62.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.62.text: Take refuge in Him alone with your whole being, O scion of the Bharata dynasty. Through His grace, you will attain supreme peace and the eternal abode.

18.62.author: Swami Sivananda
18.62.text: Fly to Him for refuge with all your being, O Arjuna; by His grace you will obtain supreme peace and the eternal abode.

18.62.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.62.text: With all your strength, fly to Him and surrender yourself, and by His grace you will attain Supreme Peace and reach the Eternal Home.

18.63.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.63.text: Thus, the path of wisdom, a better secret than all other secrets, has been expounded to you by Me; comprehend it fully and then act as you wish.

18.63.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.63.text: Thus, the knowledge, the mystery of mysteries, has been declared to you by Me. Reflecting on it fully, do as you will.

18.63.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.63.text: To you I have imparted this knowledge, which is more secret than any secret. Ponder over this as a whole and do as you like.

18.63.author: Swami Sivananda
18.63.text: Thus, wisdom more secret than secrecy itself has been declared to you by me. Reflect on it fully, then act as you wish.

18.63.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.63.text: Thus, I have revealed to you the truth, the mystery of mysteries. Having thought it over, you are free to act as you wish.

18.64.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.64.text: Yet again, you must listen to My ultimate, supreme message—the highest secret of all. You are My dear one and have a firm intellect, so I shall tell you what is good for you.

18.64.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.64.text: Hear again My supreme word, the most secret of all; as I am exceedingly fond of you, I am telling you what is good for you.

18.64.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.64.text: Listen again to My highest utterance, which is the most profound of all. Since you are ever dear to Me, I shall speak what is beneficial to you.

18.64.author: Swami Sivananda
18.64.text: Hear again My supreme word, most secret of all; for you are dearly beloved of Me, I will tell you what is good.

18.64.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.64.text: Listen to My last word once more, the deepest secret of all; you are My beloved, you are My friend, and I speak for your welfare.

18.65.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.65.text: Fix your mind on Me; be devoted to Me; offer oblations to Me and bow down to Me; you will come to Me alone. I promise you this truly, for you are dear to Me.

18.65.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.65.text: Focus your mind on Me. Be My devotee. Worship Me. Prostrate before Me. You will come to Me alone. I promise you truly; for you are dear to Me.

18.65.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.65.text: Fix your mind on Me, be devoted to Me, offer sacrifices to Me, and bow down to Me. Thus, you will come to Me alone. I promise you this truth, for you are dear to Me.

18.65.author: Swami Sivananda
18.65.text: Fix your mind on Me, be devoted to Me, sacrifice to Me, bow down to Me. You will come to Me; I truly promise you this, for you are dear to Me.

18.65.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.65.text: Dedicate yourself to Me, worship Me, sacrifice all for Me, prostrate yourself before Me, and you will surely come to Me. I truly pledge to you; you are My beloved.

18.66.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.66.text: Abandon all attributes and come to Me as your only refuge; I will rescue you from all sins; do not be sorrowful.

18.66.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.66.text: Relinquishing all Dharmas completely, seek Me alone for refuge. I will release you from all sins; grieve not.

18.66.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.66.text: Abandon all forms of rites and duties, and take refuge in Me alone. I will free you from all sins; do not grieve.

18.66.author: Swami Sivananda
18.66.text: Abandon all duties and take refuge in Me alone; I will liberate you from all sins; do not grieve.

18.66.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.66.text: Give up your earthly duties, surrender yourself to Me alone. Do not be anxious; I will absolve you from all your sins.

18.67.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.67.text: This knowledge is for you, and it should never be imparted to one who does not observe austerities; to one who has no devotion; to one who has no desire to listen; and to one who is indignant towards Me.

18.67.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.67.text: Never should this be told by you to one who is not austere, who is not a devotee, nor to one who has no desire to listen, nor certainly to him who speaks ill of Me.

18.67.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.67.text: This (that I have taught) should never be taught to one who is devoid of austerities, one who is not a devotee, one who does not render service, or one who cavils at Me.

18.67.author: Swami Sivananda
18.67.text: Never speak this to one who is devoid of austerities or devotion, who does not render service, who does not desire to listen, or who cavils at Me.

18.67.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.67.text: Do not speak this to one who has not practiced austerities, or to one who does not love, or who will not listen, or who mocks.

18.68.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.68.text: Whoever declares this highest secret to My devotees, cultivating an utmost devotion towards Me and not entertaining any doubt, shall reach Me.

18.68.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.68.text: He who proclaims this supreme mystery among My devotees shall come to Me, acquiring supreme devotion towards Me. There is no doubt about this.

18.68.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.68.text: He who, entertaining supreme devotion to Me, speaks of this highest secret to My devotees, will without doubt reach Me alone.

18.68.author: Swami Sivananda
18.68.text: He who, with supreme devotion to Me, teaches this supreme secret to My devotees, shall undoubtedly come to Me.

18.68.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.68.text: But he who teaches this great secret to My devotees, his is the highest devotion, and he shall surely come to Me.

18.69.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.69.text: And, except for him, there would be no one among men who is the best performer of what is dear to Me; and there shall be no one else dearer to Me on earth.

18.69.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.69.text: There is no one among men who does dearer service to Me than him. Nor shall there be anyone on earth dearer to Me than him.

18.69.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.69.text: And compared to him, no other human is better at accomplishing what is dear to Me. Furthermore, there will be no one else in the world dearer to Me than him.

18.69.author: Swami Sivananda
18.69.text: There is no one among men who does service dearer to Me, nor shall there be anyone on earth dearer to Me than him.

18.69.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.69.text: There is no one among men who can perform a service dearer to Me than this, nor is there any man on earth more beloved by Me than him.

18.70.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.70.text: Whoever would learn this sacred dialogue of both of us, by them I am delighted through the knowledge-sacrifice: This is my opinion.

18.70.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.70.text: And he who will study our dialogue, which is consistent with Dharma, by him I shall be worshipped through the sacrifice of knowledge; that is My view.

18.70.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.70.text: And he who will study this sacred conversation between us two, which is conducive to virtue, by him I shall be adored through the Sacrifice of Knowledge. This is My judgment.

18.70.author: Swami Sivananda
18.70.text: And he who studies this sacred dialogue of ours, by him I shall have been worshipped through the sacrifice of wisdom; such is my conviction.

18.70.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.70.text: He who will study this spiritual discourse of ours, I assure you, they shall thereby worship Me at the altar of Wisdom.

18.71.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.71.text: A man who would at least hear this with faith and without indignation—he too, freed from sins, will attain the auspicious worlds of those who have performed meritorious acts.

18.71.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.71.text: And the man who listens to it with faith and without cavil, he too shall be released and shall reach the auspicious realms of those who have performed virtuous deeds.

18.71.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.71.text: Any man who, being reverent and free from caviling, listens to this (teaching) with reverence, he too, becoming free, shall attain the blessed worlds of those who perform virtuous deeds.

18.71.author: Swami Sivananda
18.71.text: Also, the man who hears this, full of faith and free from malice, shall attain to the happy worlds of those of righteous deeds, and be liberated.

18.71.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.71.text: Yes, he who listens to it with faith and without doubt, even he, freed from evil, will rise to the worlds which the virtuous attain through righteous deeds.

18.72.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.72.text: O son of Prtha! Have you heard this with an attentive mind? O Dhananjaya! Has your strong delusion, born of ignorance, been completely destroyed?

18.72.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.72.text: Have you heard this, O Arjuna, with a single-minded focus? Has your delusion, caused by ignorance, been dispelled?

18.72.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.72.text: O Partha, have you listened to this with a one-pointed mind? O Dhananjaya, has your delusion caused by ignorance been dispelled?

18.72.author: Swami Sivananda
18.72.text: Has this been heard, O Arjuna, with one-pointed focus? Has the delusion of your ignorance been destroyed, O Dhananjaya?

18.72.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.72.text: O Arjuna, have you listened attentively to My words? Has your ignorance and delusion gone?

18.73.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.73.text: Arjuna said, "My delusion is destroyed; I have regained my recollection through your grace, O Acyuta! I stand firm, free of doubts; I shall execute your command."

18.73.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.73.text: Arjuna said, "My delusion has been destroyed, and, by Your grace, O Krsna, I have gained knowledge (Smrti). Freed from doubts, I stand steadfast, and I will fulfill Your will."

18.73.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.73.text: Arjuna said, "O Acyuta, my delusion has been destroyed and my memory has been regained through Your grace. I stand with my doubt removed; I shall follow Your instructions."

18.73.author: Swami Sivananda
18.73.text: Arjuna said, "My delusion has been destroyed, for I have gained my knowledge (memory) through Your grace, O Krishna. I am now free from doubts. I will act according to Your word."

18.73.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.73.text: Arjuna replied: "My Lord! O Immutable One! My delusion has fled. By Your Grace, O Changeless One, the light has dawned. My doubts have been dispelled, and I stand before You ready to do Your will."

18.74.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.74.text: Sanjaya said: Thus, I have heard this wonderful and thrilling dialogue between Vasudeva and the mighty-minded son of Prtha.

18.74.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.74.text: Sanjaya said, Thus I have heard this wondrous dialogue between Vasudeva and the great-minded Arjuna, which makes my hair stand on end.

18.74.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.74.text: Sanjaya said, "I thus heard this conversation between Vasudeva and the great-souled Partha, which is unique and makes one's hair stand on end."

18.74.author: Swami Sivananda
18.74.text: Sanjaya said, Thus, I have heard this wonderful dialogue between Krishna and the high-souled Arjuna, which causes one's hair to stand on end.

18.74.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.74.text: Sanjaya said: "I heard this rare, wonderful, and soul-stirring discourse between Lord Shri Krishna and the great-souled Arjuna.

18.75.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.75.text: Through the grace of Vyasa, I have heard this highly secret supreme Yoga from Krsna, the Lord of Yogis, while He was imparting it personally.

18.75.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.75.text: By the grace of Vyasa, I have heard this supreme mystery of Yoga, declared in person by Krsna, the Lord of Yoga.

18.75.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.75.text: Through the favor of Vyasa, I heard this secret concerning the supreme Yoga from Krishna, the Lord of Yogas, while He Himself was speaking!

18.75.author: Swami Sivananda
18.75.text: Through the grace of Vyasa, I have heard this supreme and most secret Yoga, directly from Krishna, the Lord of Yoga, Himself declaring it.

18.75.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.75.text: Through the blessing of the sage Vyasa, I heard this secret and noble science from the lips of its Master, Lord Shri Krishna.

18.76.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.76.text: O King! By repeatedly recollecting this wonderful, pious dialogue between Kesava and Arjuna, I am filled with delight again and again.

18.76.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.76.text: O King, remembering again and again this wondrous and auspicious dialogue between Sri Krishna and Arjuna, I rejoice time and again.

18.76.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.76.text: And, O King, while repeatedly remembering this unique, sacred dialogue between Kesava and Arjuna, I rejoice every moment.

18.76.author: Swami Sivananda
18.76.text: O King, remembering this wonderful and holy dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna, I continually rejoice.

18.76.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.76.text: O King! The more I think of that marvelous and holy discourse, the more I lose myself in joy.

18.77.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.77.text: O great king! On recalling in my mind that extremely wonderful, supreme form of Hari, I am amazed and experience joy again and again.

18.77.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.77.text: And, remembering over and over again that most marvelous form of Hari, great is my amazement, O King, and I rejoice again and again.

18.77.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.77.text: O King, repeatedly recollecting that greatly extraordinary form of Hari, I am struck with wonder and rejoice again and again.

18.77.author: Swami Sivananda
18.77.text: And, remembering again and again that most wonderful form of Hari, I am filled with great wonder, O King; and I rejoice again and again.

18.77.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.77.text: As I recall again and again the exceeding beauty of the Lord, I am filled with amazement and joy.

18.78.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
18.78.text: Where Krishna, the Lord of Yogis, remains, where the son of Prtha holds his bow, there lies fortune, victory, prosperity, and firm justice—so I believe.

18.78.author: Swami Adidevananda
18.78.text: Wherever there is Sri Krsna, the Lord of Yoga, and Arjuna the archer, there is always fortune, victory, wealth, and sound morality. This is my firm conviction.

18.78.author: Swami Gambirananda
18.78.text: Where there is Krishna, the Lord of yogas, and where there is Partha, the wielder of the bow, there is fortune, victory, prosperity, and unfailing prudence. Such is my conviction.

18.78.author: Swami Sivananda
18.78.text: Wherever Krishna, the Lord of Yoga, is; and wherever Arjuna, the wielder of the bow, is; there is prosperity, victory, happiness, and a firm policy; this is my conviction.

18.78.author: Shri Purohit Swami
18.78.text: Wherever Lord Shri Krishna, the Prince of Wisdom, and Arjuna, the Great Archer, are, I am certain that good fortune, victory, happiness, and righteousness will follow.
